title: Mobility-Gap Robustness and Středa-Hall Separation in Disordered Axion Pumping
abstract: We show that the noncommutative second Chern number of a $(3+1)$D disordered axion pump remains quantized beyond global spectral gap closure at $W_g \approx 14.5$. Large-scale computation of the second Chern number and finite-size scaling demonstrate convergence of $\mathrm{Ch}_2$ toward $-1$ well into the mobility-gap regime ($W \lesssim 16.5$), while the Středa-Hall response $\partial_φ\mathrm{Ch}_{0,3}$ departs rapidly after global spectral gap closure, serving as an internal control that distinguishes bulk mobility-gap protection from finite-size artifacts. Level statistics identify a 3D unitary Anderson transition at each pump slice and locate the mobility-edge bottleneck at $τ=0$, with critical disorder $W_c \approx 18$.
summary: This work investigates the robustness of topological quantization in a disordered 3D axion pump. The authors show that the second Chern number ($	ext{Ch}_2$) remains quantized even when the system's spectral gap closes, a phenomenon distinct from the behavior of the Středa-Hall response. This demonstrates a robust topological protection mechanism surviving deep into the mobility-gap regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates the robustness of the quantized second Chern number ($	ext{Ch}_2$) in a disordered, dynamically pumped axion insulator, specifically comparing its protection mechanism to the Středa-Hall response ($\partial\phi_{	ext{Ch}0,3}$).
main_result: The second Chern number ($	ext{Ch}_2$) remains quantized well into the mobility-gap regime beyond the global spectral gap closure, while the Středa-Hall response rapidly departs, demonstrating a distinct form of topological protection.
method: The study employs large-scale numerical computations, including the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) for calculating topological invariants and analyzing level statistics to detect Anderson transitions.
model_or_system: The system is a (3+1)D disordered axion pump, modeled as a stack of bilayer Haldane sheets with $	au$-dependent interlayer coupling. A 1D counterpart (Rice–Mele model) is also analyzed for contrast.
key_observables: Second Chern number ($	ext{Ch}_2$), Středa-Hall response ($\partial\phi_{	ext{Ch}0,3}$), Spectral Gap ($\Delta$), Level-spacing ratio ($\langle r angle$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), System size ($L$), Time/cycle parameter ($	au$), Critical disorder ($W_c \approx 18$), Global spectral gap closure ($W_g \approx 14.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations like the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) to handle large system sizes, and it distinguishes between gap-dependent and mobility-gap protection mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of $	ext{Ch}_2$ and $\partial\phi_{	ext{Ch}0,3}$ across disorder strengths, showing the separation beyond the spectral gap closure ($W_g$) and the identification of the mobility-edge bottleneck ($W_c$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and key diagnostics, then analyzes the behavior of $	ext{Ch}_2$ and $\partial\phi_{	ext{Ch}0,3}$ relative to the spectral gap closure ($W_g$). It then uses level statistics to pinpoint the mobility-edge bottleneck ($W_c$), contrasting the 3D robustness with the breakdown observed in a 1D model.
why_interesting: The concept of mobility-gap protection for topological invariants is highly relevant to understanding robust quantum states in realistic, disordered condensed matter systems, which is a key area for quantum simulation and topological quantum computing.
